questions.stem: Which one of the following is a unit of energy?
explanation_steps:
**Analysis:**
- **Joule:** The SI unit of work and energy.
- **Dyne:** A CGS unit of force.
- **Watt:** The SI unit of power.
- **Newton:** The SI unit of force.
- **Horsepower:** A non-SI unit of power.

**Result:** Joule is the correct unit for energy.

questions.stem: A particle moves in circular motion at constant speed. The acceleration of the particle is

options.A: parallel to the velocity of the particle.
options.B: directed outwards along the radius of the circular path of the particle.
options.D: directed towards the center of the circle.
options.E: variable in magnitude due to changing direction of velocity.

explanation_steps: In uniform circular motion, an object moves at a constant speed, but its direction is continuously changing. This change in direction constitutes an acceleration called **centripetal acceleration**, which is always directed **towards the center** of the circular path.

questions.stem: A ball thrown vertically upwards from the ground reaches to a maximum height and returns to the ground after some seconds. Its kinetic energy is zero

options.B: as it reaches three fourth of the maximum height.
options.C: as it reaches half of the maximum height.
options.D: as it is thrown from the ground.

explanation_steps: When a ball is thrown upwards, its velocity decreases due to gravity until it momentarily stops at the very top. Since Kinetic Energy ($$ KE = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 $$) depends on velocity, and velocity is zero at the **maximum height**, the kinetic energy is also zero at that point.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is **wrong** about nuclear force?

options.A: Nuclear force is an attractive force.
options.B: Nuclear force is very short ranged.
options.C: Nuclear force is responsible for binding the nucleons in the nucleus of an atom.
options.D: Nuclear force acts only between neutrons in the nucleus.
options.E: Nuclear force is much greater than the electrostatic force between the protons in the nucleus.

explanation_steps:
**Analysis:**
- A, B, C, E are standard properties of the strong nuclear force.
- **Choice D is wrong** because the strong nuclear force is **charge-independent**. It acts between protons and protons, neutrons and neutrons, and protons and neutrons equally.

questions.stem: Which of the following devices is used to convert light energy to electric energy?
explanation_steps: A **photo-voltaic cell** (solar cell) specifically converts light energy directly into electrical energy through the photovoltaic effect. While a photo cell (C) detects light, a PV cell is the standard term for energy conversion.

explanation_steps: When a rubber sheet is pressed onto a smooth surface, air is pushed out from underneath. The **atmospheric pressure** pushing down on the top of the sheet becomes much greater than the pressure underneath, creating a suction effect that holds it firmly.

questions.stem: The frequency of a wave is

options.A: always less than the frequency of vibration of its source.
options.B: greater than the frequency of vibration of its source.
options.C: always equal to the frequency of vibration of its source.
options.D: the number of crests that pass a given point.

explanation_steps: A wave is generated by a vibrating source. The **frequency of the wave is identical to the frequency of the source** that creates it. If a tuning fork vibrates at 440 Hz, it creates a sound wave of exactly 440 Hz.

options.A: charged particles moving at constant velocity.

explanation_steps: EM waves are produced by **accelerating charges**. An **oscillating charge** is a type of accelerating charge (it continuously changes direction and speed), which generates changing electric and magnetic fields that propagate as a wave.

questions.stem: If all vectors are parallel to each other, then they are said to be __________.
explanation_steps: Vectors that lie along the same line or on parallel lines are called **collinear** vectors. In some contexts, they are simply referred to as parallel vectors if they point in the same or opposite directions without necessarily being on the same line.

questions.stem: If a projectile is fired with horizontal velocity of 40 m/s from the top of a building, its vertical initial velocity is __________.
explanation_steps: In horizontal projection, the object is launched purely in the x-axis. Therefore, at the exact moment of launch ($$ t=0 $$), the vertical component of velocity ($$ v_{iy} $$) is **zero**.

questions.stem: The __________ states that the work done on a body is equal to the change in the kinetic energy of the body.
explanation_steps: The **Work-Energy Theorem** establishes that the net work done by all forces acting on an object equals the change in its kinetic energy ($$ W_{net} = \Delta KE $$).

questions.stem: Heat transfer mechanism that does not require a material medium is __________.
explanation_steps: **Radiation** involves energy transfer via electromagnetic waves (infrared). Unlike conduction (solids) or convection (fluids), radiation can propagate through a vacuum (empty space).

questions.stem: If the focal length of a spherical mirror is 12 cm, then its radius of curvature is __________.
explanation_steps:
The radius of curvature ($$ R $$) of a spherical mirror is twice its focal length ($$ f $$). 
**Calculation:** $$ R = 2 \times f = 2 \times 12 \text{ cm} = 24 \text{ cm} $$.

questions.stem: The magnetic moment per unit volume of a solid is known as __________.
explanation_steps: **Definition:** Magnetization ($$ M $$) is a vector field that expresses the density of permanent or induced magnetic dipole moments in a magnetic material.

questions.stem: A sound wave has an alternating pattern of __________.
explanation_steps: Sound is a longitudinal wave that travels through a medium by creating regions of high pressure (**compressions**) and low pressure (**rarefactions**).

questions.stem: For an object submerged in a fluid, the buoyant force on the object is due to the __________ between the top and bottom surfaces of the object.
explanation_steps: Pressure in a fluid increases with depth. Therefore, the pressure on the bottom of a submerged object is greater than the pressure on the top. This **pressure difference** creates an upward force called buoyancy.

questions.stem: The spectrum produced by light from a very hot molten metal is __________.
explanation_steps: Incandescent solids, liquids, or dense gases (like molten metal) emit light at all visible wavelengths, creating a **continuous spectrum** (a smooth rainbow without gaps).

questions.stem: In lenses, image is formed by __________.
explanation_steps: Lenses work by bending light rays as they pass through the transparent material. This bending of light when it enters a different medium is called **refraction**.
